issues.legal_issue: Delay in delivery of a special report to a magistrate does not, by itself, establish that the first information report was recorded later than claimed.
material_facts: The first information report was recorded in the evening, and the special report was entrusted to a constable shortly afterward for delivery to the magistrate.

The constable delivered the report the following morning and gave explanations for the delay, including a punctured bicycle tyre and stomach pain; the court did not need to accept those explanations to assess when the report was entrusted to him.
The informant was not shown to be a false witness, and the challenge to his knowledge of the injured persons’ whereabouts at the hospital had not been put to him.
issues.conclusion: The delay in delivery did not justify inferring that the first information report had not been recorded at the stated time; the challenge based on that delay was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: A delayed special report may raise a question about when the first information report was recorded, but the delay does not itself establish later recording. The inference depends on whether the informant’s account is discredited. No particular statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging criminal convictions.
predicates.special_report_delivery_delayed: A special report was delivered to the magistrate later than the time it was entrusted for delivery.
predicates.informant_not_discredited: The informant’s account of when the first information report was recorded was not shown to be false or discredited.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal involves a delayed special report but the informant is not discredited, the delay alone does not establish that the first information report was recorded later.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to prove an alleged part of an attack beyond reasonable doubt does not necessarily discredit the remaining prosecution evidence when that part is not found false and other evidence supports the assault.
material_facts: The prosecution witnesses described firing during the attack, but the High Court found that firing had not been proved beyond reasonable doubt.
The High Court did not affirmatively find that the firing account was false, and the evidence did not rule out the possibility that some assailants fired weapons.
The eyewitnesses consistently described firing, while the other alleged assailants’ weapons and the evidence of the attack provided support independent of whether firing occurred.
The appeal challenged the remaining convictions on the ground that the firing account was integral to the prosecution case.
issues.conclusion: The failure to prove firing beyond reasonable doubt did not require rejection of the rest of the prosecution case, and the convictions challenged in the appeal were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: A failure to establish one part of the prosecution account beyond reasonable doubt is not equivalent to an affirmative finding that the account is false; the remaining evidence must be assessed on its own. No particular statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and alleged_firing_not_proved_beyond_reasonable_doubt and alleged_firing_not_found_false and other_evidence_supports_assault

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging criminal convictions.
predicates.alleged_firing_not_proved_beyond_reasona: The prosecution’s allegation that firearms were used was not established beyond reasonable doubt.
predicates.alleged_firing_not_found_false: The court did not affirmatively find that the allegation of firing was false.
predicates.other_evidence_supports_assault: Other evidence, including eyewitness accounts and evidence of injuries caused by other weapons, supported the alleged assault apart from whether firing occurred.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, when firing is not proved but is not found false and other evidence supports the assault, that failure alone does not discredit the remaining prosecution evidence.
